source.title: Interpretable Safety Alignment via SAE-Constructed Low-Rank Subspace Adaptation
source.authors: Dian-Yun Wang; Qing-Sen Ma; Yu-Hu Shang; Zhi-Feng Lu; Lechen Ning; Zhenbo Xu; Hui-Jia Wu; Zhao-Feng He

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE-identified features in an LLM have causal effects using activation scaling, a different method from the toy-model geometry studied in the original source.
record.gate_note: The causal activation-steering experiment is a result about SAE-recovered features in a real model. The safety-alignment benchmark comparisons, layer/rank ablations, theoretical recovery bounds, and cited results are not rows: they do not directly measure the claim versions. Table 4 gives representative feature examples but does not report a separate measured outcome for each example.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained Gemma Scope and Llama Scope SAEs as a tool to build LoRA initialisation subspaces, and it reports that method's safety performance. The steering experiment only checks that its own selected features change Perspective toxicity. It does not measure whether the model spreads features across neurons or whether a dictionary recovers sparse features. The theory takes superposition and SAE monosemanticity as assumptions; it does not test them.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' central conclusion is that SAILS, an SAE-decoder-initialised LoRA, closes the gap between parameter-efficient fine-tuning and RLHF-level safety alignment (up to 99.6% safe rate on Gemma-2-9B at 0.19% of parameters) while adding interpretability. The steering experiment and the recovery-error theorems are offered as supporting validation.
record.recipe_differences: This is an SAE-guided safety-alignment and activation-steering study, not a reproduction of the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation scaling factor changes toxicity; the steering experiment uses layer 15 and the top-50 identified features.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling activations of the top-50 selected safety SAE features at layer 15 in Gemma-2-2B changes Perspective toxicity in both directions: amplification lowers it from 0.42 to 0.28 at γ=2.5, and suppression raises it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrast-selected SAE features in an LLM causally steer safety-relevant output behaviour.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The causal steering evaluation uses a subset of harmful prompts whose size is not stated. Only the baseline and γ = 2.5 toxicity values are given in text; the other scaling-condition values are figure-only. The experiment tests selected features in one model and does not establish completeness or generality of SAE features.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcome rows were left out. Safety-alignment benchmark results and subspace/rank/width ablations were omitted because they measure SAILS performance rather than the claim versions' representational properties.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of the capacity-competition explanation; the study only assumes it in its framing.
SAE recoverability and distributed features are assumed (Assumption 2, Definition 1), not measured. The steering result only validates the method's feature selection.
Completeness, stability and canonicity are not tested. The 16K vs 65K width ablation is a downstream safety metric only; the feature-splitting explanation is the authors' speculation.

record.verdict_notes: The study assumes superposition (it cites Elhage et al.) and SAE monosemanticity as theoretical premises. Its theorems derive from those assumptions and give no empirical evidence about them. The record's reader labelled V4 'supports', but the steering result validates the method's own feature selection on a downstream toxicity score, so no verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular overlap geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure or whether it is evidence of superposition.
Tests causal effects of selected SAE features in one model and setting; does not measure feature distribution across neurons or establish coverage across the model's representations.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units. It notes limitations of auto-generated explanations and perturbation of the adapted subspace.
Does not test whether individual superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selected SAE safety features in Gemma-2-2B, layer 15, on the tested harmful prompts
reader_labels.reason: Scaling the selected features changes toxicity in both directions, with amplification reducing it from 0.42 to 0.28 at γ = 2.5; this supports causal influence of SAE-recovered features in this setting (R1–R6).
